newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: ATHLETICS-NEBIOLO HINTS AT RADICAL CHANGES TO GRAND PRIX CIRCUIT.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-NEBIOLO HINTS AT RADICAL CHANGES TO GRAND PRIX CIRCUIT.

text.p: World athletics chief Primo Nebiolo hinted on Thursday at radical changes to the grand prix circuit from 1998 with a reduction in the number of meetings.
"We don't have difficulty with having great meetings on the grand prix," Nebiolo told a news conference after the International Amateur Athletic Federation's (IAAF) annual calendar meeting.
"The difficulty is to stop the number, if it will be possible to have a great super league."
Nebiolo did not elaborate on the format of a new super league but IAAF sources said he apparently wanted a smaller circuit of elite meetings.
In a statement released after the news conference, the IAAF president said the 1997 circuit would be the last in the present form.
"We must find new ways of packaging and presenting the circuit so as to stimulate the public; by athletes, the media and the sponsors," the statement said.
"The IAAF is studying a new concept and philosophy for the 1998 grand prix and the IAAF grand prix commission will meet again in April to discuss and propose details."
For the first time next year prize money will be available at the world indoor championships scheduled for Paris from March 7-9 and at the world outdoor championships in Athens from August 1-10.

Almost $4 million in prize money will be available at the grand prix final in Fukuoka, Japan, on September 13, the first time the final has been staged outside Europe since the circuit started 11 years ago.
"We want to offer a certain opportunity to the athletes," Nebiolo said. "This is not professionalism, professionalism implies a given salary and a guaranteed pension.
"We don't have the resources for that but we can't forget the athletes."
